prerequisites.description: Resolving components is necessary to construct equilibrium force balance equations.
Equilibrium FBD is the required prerequisite for accelerated dynamic frame analysis.
Normal reaction determination from NLM is required to calculate limiting friction.
Work-energy theorem integrates Newton's second law over path displacement.
Potential energy formulation requires understanding work done by conservative forces.
Energy conservation in harmonic oscillators links potential and kinetic energy phase space.
Understanding function domain and asymptotic behavior is necessary for evaluating limits.
Continuity is strictly defined through limit equality: LHL = RHL = f(a).
A function must be continuous to be differentiable; derivative limits rely on continuity.
Monotonicity and extremum detection require computing and signing first/second derivatives.
Indefinite integration is the anti-derivative reverse operation.
Definite integration applies fundamental calculus theorems over indefinite primitives.
Area calculation integrates bounded regions using definite integration limits.
Enthalpy delta H from First Law is required to calculate Gibbs Free Energy delta G.
Spontaneity relation delta G_0 = -RT ln K connects thermodynamics with equilibrium.
Ionic equilibrium applies mass action equilibrium laws to weak electrolyte systems.
Electron-withdrawing -M/-I effects at ortho/para positions lower activation barrier for nucleophilic attack.
